A metal, Y belongs to group 2 of the periodic table on the basis of this information, answer the following questions:
a) Give the chemical formula of the possible oxide of Y.
b) Suggest the expected bond type in the oxide.
c) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of the metal oxide with water.
d) Write an equation for the effect of adding aqueous hydrogen chloride to the aqueous solution obtained in (c) above.

Explain the following:
a) Tin and lead have variable oxidation states and form complex ion but are not regarded as transition metals. (2 marks)

a) Outline two similarities between electrochemical and electrolytic cells. (2 marks)
b) In a tabular form, state four differences between electrochemical and electrolytic cells. (4 marks)

(i) With suitable reason, which of the metals will serve as the cathode and the anode? (2 marks)

(vi) Is the reaction spontaneous? Explain (2 marks)

At $200\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$, the $K_c$ for the reaction
$$\text{PCl}_{5(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_{3(g)} + \text{Cl}_{2(g)} \quad \Delta H = +124\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
has a numerical value of $8 \times 10^{-3}$.
a) Write an expression for $K_c$ in terms of the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) and the total volume (V) (3 marks)
b) What is the unit of $K_c$? (2 marks)
c)(i) What is the value of $K_c$ for the reverse reaction at the same temperature in terms of $\alpha$ and V? (2 marks)
(ii) Write the unit for the reverse reaction. (1 mark)
d) What will be the effect of $K_c$ if:
(i) more $\text{PCl}_5$ is added (ii) pressure is increased (iii) temperature is increased? (2 marks)
e) Predict the effect on the equilibrium composition if:
(i) more $\text{PCl}_5$ is added; (2 marks)
(ii) pressure is increased; (2 marks)
(iii) temperature is increased. (2 marks)
f) At $200\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ and a total pressure of $1\text{ atmosphere}$, the $\text{PCl}_5$ is found to be $50\%$ dissociated. Write an expression for the $K_p$ in terms of $\alpha$ and $P$. Calculate the equilibrium constant $K_p$ at this temperature. (9 marks)
